name: addon-reviewer: `backfilledAt` in the adopted-release diagnosis no longer says when the one-time derivation ran
description:
Follow-up to PR 71 (`shoptet/aidev-apps`), which made the publication backfill a step of the deploy (`Backfill publication` in the `addon-reviewer` workflow, after `Verify`). PR 71 merged on 2026-09-29 (merge commit `3ddfb92`) and its deploy went green.

This ticket opened with four items. Three are closed — what happened to each is at the end — and one is left.

## `carried_over_backfilled_at` no longer says when the derivation ran

`markCarriedOverBackfilled` is called at the end of every run (`packages/db/src/backfill-published.ts:343`, held by the test "records that it ran, even with nothing to stamp"), so the value is the last successful backfill — which, since PR 71, is usually just the last deploy.

Every production reader treats it as a boolean, verified against all five: the kill-switch guard (`apps/console/lib/admin-actions.ts:331`), `assertRequeueSafeToReset` (`packages/db/src/reviews-write.ts:425`), the backfill's own two reads (`backfill-published.ts:186` and `:378`), and the console's published-count fallback, which names its variable `backfilledAt` but only branches on it (`apps/console/lib/queries.ts:1082`).

One reader lets the value out. `apps/worker/src/jobs/outbound-send.ts:694` logs it as `backfilledAt` in the adopted-release diagnosis — the one place an operator is actively asking when the one-time derivation ran, and the field name reads as if it answered that. The message beside it is not affected: `repair` branches on the same value as a boolean and says the right thing either way.

PR 71 documented the trap (`docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md`) rather than fixing it. The fix is either to drop the field from that log line, or to add a second key holding the derivation's own timestamp.

It is not dead code, even though production currently holds nothing that could reach it (see the premise check below). The adopted path skips `setPublishedCommentIds` (`outbound-send.ts:455-487` — "a crash-adopted retry never runs the composer at all"), so a send adopted after a crash reaches `sent` with `published_comment_ids = NULL` and lands exactly here.

**Done when:** an operator reading the adopted-release diagnosis cannot mistake the last backfill for the date of the one-time derivation — either because the field is gone, or because it is named for what it holds and the derivation's own date sits beside it.

## Premise check: answered on 2026-09-29, nothing left to run

The original description ended with a `qm guest exec` query to be run from erebor, because items 1 and 3 depended on what production holds. The first deploy carrying the step ([run 36577470157](https://github.com/shoptet/aidev-apps/actions/runs/36577470157)) answered it without the VM:

> `publication backfilled: 0 sent releases (0 from their own recorded set, none re-derived), 0 comments stamped, 0 releases with no review row`

`backfillPublished` counts the same rows that query did — `outbound_messages` on `event = 'findings_release' and status = 'sent'` (`backfill-published.ts:152-166`) — so `sent_total = 0`, and `legacy = 0` follows. Production has never sent a findings release. Nothing was there for the one-time derivation to recover and nothing was stamped approximately, and the marker is set either way, so the kill-switch guard and `assertRequeueSafeToReset` are satisfied.

## What happened to the other three

**1. The one-time derivation is not transactional** — done, under CZ3TDR1-738. PR 79 (commit `e40292f`) put the derivation and its stamp into a single `db.transaction` behind `pg_advisory_xact_lock`, which also covers a run started on top of a still-working orphan. Two tests in `packages/db/src/backfill-published.test.ts` cover the interrupted run ("a run that dies midway derives nothing and leaves the derivation unretired" and "a deriving run that dies takes an exact repair down with it"), and the trade against holding locks on `review_comments` while the live worker writes to the same table is written down beside `timeout-minutes: 10`. PR 79 merged into PR 71's branch and reached master with it.

**2. The backfill cannot be run without a full deploy** — closed by the same commit, as the "or the decision not to is written down" half of the old Done when. `workflow_dispatch` is on the workflow. It starts the whole deploy rather than the backfill alone, and the trigger's comment records why there is no input to skip the build: the build is cache-warm and `compose up` on unchanged images is a no-op, so a backfill-only route would save little and cost a second, rarely-exercised path through that file.

**3. "LEFT UNTOUCHED" becomes a permanent fixture of every deploy log** — dropped. `legacy = 0` settles the complaint: in the steady state the clause has nothing to count, so it is a fixture of nothing. It is not unreachable, though, which makes the rule written here originally — "legacy = 0 means item 3 can never fire" — wrong: a crash-adopted send creates a row it would count, and that is exactly the diagnosis the clause was written for. So it goes away as a noise complaint and the wording stands as it is.
